acl.description: Principals (emails or prefixed principals) allowed to read objects synced from this resource. Absent means unrestricted; provider permissions take precedence where supported.

acl_warning.description: Why this resource's permissions could not be read. Without an access rule of yours, its objects are readable by everyone meanwhile; with one, your rule applies. Clears on the next successful read.

acl_warning_at.description: When `acl_warning` last changed (RFC 3339). An unchanged warning keeps its original time.

additional_metadata.description: Key-value pairs merged into the additional metadata (`additional_metadata`) of every object synced from this resource. Provider-generated fields win on conflict.

backfill_error.description: Most recent failure fetching historical records. Cleared when progress resumes.

backfill_error_at.description: When the historical fetch last failed, in RFC3339 format.

backfill_oldest.description: Oldest point (RFC 3339) the background fetch of older history has reached. Empty when that fetch is finished or not needed.

collection_override.description: Routes this resource's synced objects into a specific collection, overriding the connector's. Formerly `sub_tenant_id_override`.

custom_instructions.description: Ingestion and indexing instructions for this resource, replacing the connector's `custom_instructions`; empty inherits it. Up to 4000 characters, applied from the next sync.

database_override.description: Database this resource's synced objects are routed to. Empty means the connector's own database.

metadata.description: Key-value pairs merged into the metadata (`metadata`) of every object synced from this resource. The system fields `connector_id` and `provider` always win on conflict.

page_acl_warning.description: Set when page-level restrictions in this resource (for example Confluence pages) could not be resolved, so those pages are readable by everyone. Clears after a clean full sync.

provider_cursor.description: Bookmark of the last synced position. Non-empty value confirms the first sync has run.

provider_metadata.description: Additional provider-supplied metadata for this resource.

resource_id.description: Resource identifier from the Discover endpoint.

resource_type.description: Provider resource type, such as `channel`, `repository`, or `linear_team`.

status.description: Current sync state of this resource (e.g. `active`, `paused`).

sync_blocked.description: `true` when syncing stopped because the provider keeps refusing this resource, for example a deleted table or an inaccessible channel. `sync_blocked_reason` says why.

sync_blocked_at.description: When syncing of this resource was stopped (RFC 3339). Present only while `sync_blocked` is `true`.

sync_blocked_reason.description: The provider's explanation for why this resource is blocked. Present only while `sync_blocked` is `true`.

total.description: Total number of results across all pages.

answer.description: The answer you expected: the text a correct system would have produced from the retrieved context. At most 8,000 characters.

source_ids.description: The `context_id`s that actually contain the answer, as returned by /query. At most 100.

collection.description: Optional collection scope for this feedback. A collection is scoped to a database, so `database` must be sent alongside it; sending `collection` on its own is rejected.

database.description: Owning database. Formerly `tenant_id`; the `tenant_id` alias is still accepted (deprecated).

feedback.description: Free-text comment describing what was right or wrong about the results. Required unless `ground_truth` is supplied.

ground_truth.description: The known right answer: an expected `answer`, the `source_ids` that contain it, or both. When sent, `feedback` becomes optional.

metadata.description: Free-form key-value context stored alongside the feedback (e.g. agent name, conversation or eval-run ID).

rating.description: Optional overall judgement: `positive`, `negative`, or `neutral`. Omit to send a comment with no rating.

request_id.description: The `request_id` from `meta` of the query this feedback is about. Required: it links the feedback to the query that ran.

created_at.description: RFC3339 timestamp when the feedback was recorded.

feedback_id.description: Unique identifier assigned to this feedback submission.

recorded.description: Whether the feedback was durably stored.

info.description: The HydraDB API: ingest context, query it, and manage databases, connectors and webhooks.
info.title: HydraDB Application API

get.description: List all connectors for the authenticated org, optionally filtered by provider.

parameters.description: Comma-separated extras. health adds each connector's health rollup; any other value is rejected with 400.
parameters.name: include

post.description: Create a connector for a provider and store its credentials. `enforce_acl` defaults to false when omitted, so writers may create connectors without choosing the setting. Only a workspace owner in a human dashboard session may explicitly set it, and true is accepted only when the provider catalog reports acl_supported. When true, content reads always use the authenticated caller; when false, request `acl` remains an opt-in filter.

403.description: Setting enforce_acl requires a workspace owner in a signed-in dashboard session.

get.description: Lists the providers you can connect, including whether ACL capture is supported (`acl_supported`) and its summary (`acl_description`). With `id`, describes one provider: its searchable object types and fields (with `filter_key`), `credential_schema`, and `setup_guide` when needed.

parameters.description: Provider name (e.g. slack, gmail). Omit to list all.
parameters.name: id

get.summary: List supported providers, or describe one in detail

delete.description: Delete a connector, its resources, and stored credentials.

get.description: Fetch a single connector by ID.

patch.description: Update the supplied connector settings. Use `credentials` to reconnect, `sync_interval_seconds` to change cadence, `custom_instructions` to change ingestion instructions, or `enforce_acl` to set the owner-only enforcement mode. True requires provider catalog `acl_supported`; when enabled, content reads use the authenticated caller, while false keeps request `acl` as an opt-in filter.

403.description: Setting enforce_acl requires a workspace owner in a signed-in dashboard session.

409.description: The ACL enforcement revision changed after the connector was loaded; reload and retry. If the connector was deleted, the handler returns 404.

503.description: The provider capability catalog is unavailable; retry the request.

post.description: Activate the listed resources and start a sync. Unlisted resources remain unchanged. Send each listed resource's name, type, database and collection.

get.description: List a connected provider's resources using the connector's stored credentials. `cursor` or `limit` paginates (currently Notion only); continue while `has_more` is `true`.

parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response's next_cursor
parameters.name: cursor

parameters.description: Max resources per page, 1-100 (values above 100 are clamped)
parameters.name: limit

post.description: Pause scheduled syncs. An active sync stops at its next step. Resume continues from the saved position. Returns `409` if already paused.

get.description: List the configured resources for a connector.

post.description: Add a resource to the connector. An existing `resource_id` returns `409`. Use the resource PATCH endpoint to change its settings.

delete.description: Remove a resource mapping from a connector.

patch.description: Update resource instructions or access rules. Send at least one field. Omitted fields keep their values; provider permissions apply again at the next sync.
patch.summary: Update a resource's ACL rule or custom instructions

post.description: Resume a paused connector and schedule a sync immediately. Each resource continues from its saved position. Returns `409` if the connector is not paused.

get.description: Check whether a connector is working, in one call: an overall `status` plus one health entry per configured resource. Use it to find a failing resource or a connector that needs you to reconnect.

post.description: Start a sync now. If one is running, it continues and `run_id` is empty. Returns `409` while paused or when no resources are active.

delete.description: Delete contexts by ID. By default every outcome is `200`, so check `deleted_count` and `results`. Send `X-HydraDB-Delete-Status: strict` for `404`, `409` or `500` on failure.

parameters.description: `strict` answers `404`, `409` or `500` when the delete did not happen; `legacy` always answers `200`. Omit it for the server default, currently `legacy`.
parameters.name: X-HydraDB-Delete-Status

404.description: Strict mode only. No source matched the given ids; `data` carries the same results/deleted_count payload a 200 carries

409.description: Strict mode only. Source is still indexing; retry after ingestion completes (see Retry-After). `data` carries the same results/deleted_count payload a 200 carries

500.description: Strict mode only. A store failed to delete the source; the delete is retryable. `data` carries the same results/deleted_count payload a 200 carries

post.description: Ingest documents, app knowledge or memories using a multipart form. Select `knowledge` or `memory` with `type`. Poll `GET /context/status` with the returned IDs.

app_knowledge.description: App knowledge entries to ingest, encoded as a JSON array.
app_knowledge.title: app_knowledge

collection.description: Collection to write to. Omit it to use the database's default collection.
collection.title: collection

database.description: Database to write to. Required.
database.title: database

document_metadata.description: Per-file metadata for uploaded documents, encoded as JSON.
document_metadata.title: document_metadata

documents.description: Files to ingest into the knowledge corpus.
documents.title: documents

graph_payload.description: Your own graph, encoded as JSON and keyed by source ID.
graph_payload.title: graph_payload

memories.description: Memories to ingest, encoded as a JSON array. Use `type=memory`.
memories.title: memories

upsert.description: Default `upsert` for every context: replace an existing context with the same `context_id`. One of `true`, `false`, `1` or `0`; default `true`.
upsert.title: upsert

requestBody.description: A multipart form containing the database, collection and content to ingest.

415.description: Body is neither multipart/form-data nor application/json

get.description: Return the stored content of one context, its enrichment, and a time-limited download URL.

parameters.description: The ID of the context to inspect.
parameters.name: id

parameters.description: Database the context belongs to. Required.
parameters.name: database

parameters.description: Collection the context belongs to. Omit it to use the database's default collection.
parameters.name: collection

parameters.description: Lifetime of `presigned_url` in seconds, from 60 to 604800 (7 days). Default 3600.
parameters.name: expiry_seconds

parameters.description: What to return: `content` (the stored content and enrichment), `url` (a download URL only) or `both`. Default `both`.
parameters.name: mode

parameters.description: Principals to inspect as. For directly ingested knowledge and non-enforced connector content, only contexts visible to these principals can be inspected; a context that is not visible returns `404`. Enforced connector content uses the authenticated caller instead. Repeat or comma-separate values. If sent and overridden, one `meta.warnings` entry has code `acl_ignored_by_connector_enforcement`.
parameters.name: acl

post.description: List the contexts in a database or collection, ingested or synced, one page at a time. Fetch a context's content with `GET /context/inspect`.

get.description: Return the entity relations extracted from one context, or from the whole collection when `id` is omitted, with the structural graph around them. Paged by `limit` and `cursor`.

parameters.description: Collection to read. Defaults to the database's default collection.
parameters.name: collection

parameters.description: `context_id` of the context whose relations to return. Omit it for relations across the whole collection.
parameters.name: id

parameters.description: Corpus to read, `knowledge` or `memory`. Defaults to `knowledge`.
parameters.name: type

parameters.description: Maximum number of relation groups to return, from `1` to `10000`. Default `5000`.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: The `next_cursor` from the previous page, passed back unchanged. Omit it for the first page.
parameters.name: cursor

parameters.description: Principals to answer as. For directly ingested knowledge and non-enforced connector content, only results visible to these principals are returned. Enforced connector content uses the authenticated caller instead. Repeat the parameter or send a comma-separated list. If sent and overridden, one `meta.warnings` entry has code `acl_ignored_by_connector_enforcement`.
parameters.name: acl

get.description: Return the processing status of one or more contexts by ID, including contexts synced by a connector.

parameters.description: Context IDs as repeated params (`ids=a&ids=b`) or one comma-joined value (`ids=a,b`). Whitespace is trimmed; empty and duplicate entries are dropped.
parameters.name: ids

parameters.description: Database the contexts belong to. Required.
parameters.name: database

parameters.description: Collection the contexts belong to. Omit it to use the database's default collection.
parameters.name: collection

get.description: Return the contexts reachable from one context through context-level relations, up to `depth` hops, with their relations and surrounding graph.

parameters.description: The `context_id` to start from. This form takes any id, including one that contains `/`.
parameters.name: id

parameters.description: Collection to read. Defaults to the database's default collection.
parameters.name: collection

parameters.description: Corpus to read, `knowledge` or `memory`. Defaults to `knowledge`.
parameters.name: type

parameters.description: Maximum number of hops to traverse from the start context, from `1` to `10`. Default `5`.
parameters.name: depth

parameters.description: Maximum number of member contexts to return, from `1` to `1000`. Default `200`. `is_truncated` is `true` when this cut the traversal short.
parameters.name: max_sources

parameters.description: Principals to answer as. For directly ingested knowledge and non-enforced connector content, only contexts visible to these principals are returned, checked at every hop. Enforced connector content uses the authenticated caller instead. Repeat or comma-separate values. If sent and overridden, one `meta.warnings` entry has code `acl_ignored_by_connector_enforcement`.
parameters.name: acl

patch.description: Update one context without re-ingesting it: merge its metadata and additional metadata, or replace its access-control list. `database` and `collection` are required.

get.description: Get the connected subgraph of one context.

parameters.description: Context ID to start from. Use the query form for IDs containing a slash.
parameters.name: id

parameters.description: Corpus to read, `knowledge` or `memory`. Defaults to `knowledge`.
parameters.name: type

parameters.description: Max members returned; `is_truncated` reports when this clipped the traversal
parameters.name: max_sources

parameters.description: Principals allowed to read the returned contexts. For directly ingested knowledge and non-enforced connector content, only contexts visible to these principals are returned. Enforced connector content uses the authenticated caller instead for every returned context. If sent and overridden, one `meta.warnings` entry has code `acl_ignored_by_connector_enforcement`.
parameters.name: acl
